title: Uddhava Arrives in Vrindavan Bearing Krishna's Message
one_line_summary: Uddhava arrives in Vrindavan as Krishna's envoy; the gopis, pining for Krishna, surround him and ask why he has come.
source_excerpt: The astonished gopis surrounded him, asking 'Who is this of wondrous beauty, wearing Achyuta's dress and ornaments?' They recognized him as a messenger sent by Krishna for love of his parents. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-9)

title: The Gopi's Lament to the Bee (Bhramara-gita)
one_line_summary: A gopi, seeing a honeybee, addresses it as Krishna's messenger and reproaches Krishna for abandoning the gopis.
source_excerpt: 'O bee, friend of the cheat, do not touch my feet... he who made us drink the nectar of his lips once now abandons us like flowers cast aside.' The gopis sing and weep, remembering Krishna's boyhood and youthful deeds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 10-20)

title: Uddhava Delivers Krishna's Message and the Gopis Reply
one_line_summary: Uddhava conveys Krishna's teaching of unbroken spiritual union; the gopis answer that they cannot forget Krishna.
source_excerpt: Krishna's message: 'My separation from you is never complete, as ether, air, fire, water and earth pervade all beings... fix your mind wholly on me and you will soon attain me.' The gopis reply that every river, hill and forest reminds them of Krishna and they cannot forget him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 21-51)

title: Uddhava Praises the Gopis and Departs
one_line_summary: Uddhava extols the gopis' supreme devotion, wishes to be a shrub in Vrindavan, stays some months, then returns to Mathura.
source_excerpt: Uddhava declared: 'May I become any shrub, creeper or herb in Vrindavan, blessed by the dust of these gopis' feet.' After consoling Nanda, Yashoda and the gopas, he departed and returned to Mathura. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 52-68)

title: Krishna Blesses Trivakra (Sairandhri)
one_line_summary: Krishna visits the hunchback woman Trivakra, accepts her hospitality, and grants her a boon, honoring her devotion.
source_excerpt: Knowing the desire of the love-tormented Sairandhri, the Lord went to her house; she arose, adorned herself, and approached him; Krishna granted her the boon she wished and returned to his own abode. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-10)

title: Krishna Sends Akrura to Hastinapura
one_line_summary: Krishna visits Akrura's home and dispatches him to Hastinapura to learn whether the Pandavas are treated justly.
source_excerpt: Krishna told Akrura: 'Go to Gajasahvaya (Hastinapura) and learn how the Pandavas, brought there with their mother after their father's death, are faring; the blind king follows his wicked son.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-35)

title: Kunti Confides Her Sorrow to Akrura
one_line_summary: In Hastinapura, Kunti tearfully tells Akrura of the Pandavas' persecution and prays to Krishna for protection.
source_excerpt: Weeping, Kunti said: 'Krishna, Krishna, great yogin, soul of the universe, protect me who am sinking with my children; I see no refuge but your lotus feet.' Akrura and Vidura consoled her. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-14)

title: Akrura Counsels Dhritarashtra
one_line_summary: Akrura advises Dhritarashtra to treat the Pandavas as his own sons, then returns and reports to Krishna and Balarama.
source_excerpt: Akrura told the king: 'Act with fairness toward the Pandavas and your own sons; no one dwells here forever.' Dhritarashtra admitted the truth but confessed his mind was unsteady from love for his sons; Akrura then returned and reported all to Krishna and Rama. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 15-30)

title: Jarasandha Besieges Mathura
one_line_summary: Kamsa's widows report to Jarasandha, who vows to destroy the Yadavas and besieges Mathura with twenty-three armies.
source_excerpt: Kamsa's widows Asti and Prapti went to their father Jarasandha and told him of their widowhood; enraged, he resolved to make the earth Yadava-free and besieged Mathura from all sides with twenty-three akshauhinis. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-5)

title: Divine Chariot and Weapons Descend for Krishna
one_line_summary: As Krishna deliberates, a divine chariot and celestial weapons descend from the sky; Krishna and Balarama ride out to battle.
source_excerpt: While Krishna reflected, two chariots with the splendor of the sun descended from the sky with drivers and ancient divine weapons; Krishna blew his conch and terror entered the enemy's hearts. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 6-15)

title: Krishna and Balarama Rout Jarasandha's Army
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama annihilate Jarasandha's host; Balarama seizes Jarasandha, but Krishna releases him to fight again.
source_excerpt: Balarama seized the chariotless Jarasandha like a lion seizing a lion, but Krishna stayed the binding, saying 'The Magadha is not to be slain; he will gather forces again.' Seventeen times Jarasandha attacked and was routed. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 16-41)

title: Krishna Founds the City of Dvaraka
one_line_summary: Facing Kalayavana and Jarasandha together, Krishna builds the fortress-city of Dvaraka in the sea and relocates the Yadavas.
source_excerpt: Krishna built a fortress twelve yojanas wide within the sea, wondrous in every way, and by his mystic power conveyed all the people there; Indra sent the Sudharma hall and the Parijata tree, Varuna swift white horses. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 42-56)

title: Kalayavana Is Burned by Muchukunda's Glance
one_line_summary: Krishna lures Kalayavana into Muchukunda's cave; the Yavana kicks the sleeping king and is reduced to ashes.
source_excerpt: Pursued by the Yavana, Krishna entered the mountain cave; the fool kicked the sleeping man thinking him Krishna, and Muchukunda, opening his eyes, burned Kalayavana to ashes with the fire of his glance. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-11)

title: Muchukunda's Story
one_line_summary: Muchukunda, an Ikshvaku king who once guarded the gods against the asuras, was granted deep sleep as his reward.
source_excerpt: Muchukunda, son of Mandhata of the Ikshvaku line, guarded the gods in battle against the asuras; when they released him, he chose sleep as his boon and lay in the cave. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 12-20)

title: Krishna Grants Muchukunda His Boon
one_line_summary: Krishna reveals himself to Muchukunda, who renounces all boons and asks only for devotion; Krishna grants him liberation in a future birth.
source_excerpt: Recognizing Narayana, Muchukunda prayed for nothing but Krishna's service, renouncing all heavenly rewards; Krishna granted that in his next birth he would become a brahmana and attain him alone. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 21-62)

title: Krishna and Balarama Elude Jarasandha
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama feign flight from Jarasandha, escape to Dvaraka over the sea, and Jarasandha falsely believes them burned.
source_excerpt: Pursued by Jarasandha, Krishna and Rama fled on foot and climbed Mt. Pravarshana; Jarasandha set fire to the hill, but the two leapt down eleven yojanas and returned unseen to their sea-girt city, while Jarasandha wrongly believed them burned. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-13)

title: Rukmini Resolves to Marry Krishna and Sends a Brahmana Messenger
one_line_summary: Princess Rukmini, hearing of Krishna's virtues, resolves to wed him and sends a brahmana to Dvaraka with her secret message.
source_excerpt: Rukmini, daughter of Bhishmaka of Vidarbha, heard of Krishna's beauty and virtues and resolved he alone was a fitting husband; though her brother Rukmi wished to give her to Shishupala, she sent a trusted brahmana swiftly to Dvaraka. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-27)

title: Rukmini's Love-Message to Krishna
one_line_summary: Rukmini's message begs Krishna to carry her away in the rakshasa manner before Shishupala can claim her.
source_excerpt: Rukmini's message: 'You I have chosen as my husband; come and take my hand before Shishupala, like a jackal, seizes the lion's share. Tomorrow is my marriage; carry me away by the rakshasa rite, defeating the hosts of Shishupala and Jarasandha.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 28-42)

title: Krishna Hastens to Kundina
one_line_summary: Krishna receives Rukmini's message and races overnight to Kundina, where rival kings are gathering to enforce Shishupala's claim.
source_excerpt: Hearing the message, Krishna said 'I too cannot sleep at night for her'; he set out at once and reached Vidarbha in a single night, while Shishupala, Jarasandha, Shalva and other hostile kings gathered in Kundina resolved to fight if Krishna came. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-20)

title: Rukmini's Prayer at the Temple of Ambika
one_line_summary: Anxious at Krishna's delay, Rukmini visits the temple of goddess Ambika and prays that Krishna alone may be her husband.
source_excerpt: As the wedding hour neared, Rukmini, not seeing Krishna arrive, prayed tearfully; going in procession to the temple of Bhavani, she bowed: 'May Krishna, the Lord, alone become my husband; bless this.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 20-52)

title: Krishna Carries Off Rukmini at the Svayamvara
one_line_summary: Krishna seizes Rukmini as she leaves the temple, places her on his chariot, and rides off before the assembled kings.
source_excerpt: As Rukmini, having worshipped, came out of the temple and was about to mount her chariot, Krishna seized her and placed her on his own chariot, and went away slowly, breaking through the circle of kings like a lion carrying off his share from the midst of jackals. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 52-56)

title: Krishna Defeats Rukmi and Spares Him at Rukmini's Plea
one_line_summary: Krishna's forces rout the pursuing kings; Rukmi chases alone, and Krishna defeats and disfigures him but spares his life at Rukmini's entreaty.
source_excerpt: Krishna's host routed the pursuing kings; Rukmi, vowing not to re-enter Kundina without slaying Krishna, overtook him alone; Krishna cut down every weapon Rukmi raised, and as he was about to slay him, Rukmini fell at his feet and begged for her brother's life, so Krishna only shaved and disfigured him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-35)

title: Krishna Marries Rukmini in Dvaraka
one_line_summary: Rukmi founds the city of Bhojakata, and Krishna formally weds Rukmini in Dvaraka amid citywide celebration.
source_excerpt: The disgraced Rukmi built the city of Bhojakata, vowing not to return to Kundina; Krishna brought Rukmini to Dvaraka and wed her with full rites, and there was a great festival in every house of the Yadu city. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 35-59)

title: Pradyumna Is Born and Cast into the Sea by Shambara
one_line_summary: Pradyumna, Kama reborn as Krishna's son, is abducted as a newborn by the asura Shambara and thrown into the sea.
source_excerpt: Pradyumna was born to Rukmini of Krishna's potency; knowing him as his destined enemy, the shape-shifting Shambara stole the newborn and threw him into the ocean. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-2)

title: Mayavati (Rati) Rescues and Raises Pradyumna
one_line_summary: A fish swallows the infant; a cook finds him, and Mayavati, who is Rati, recognizes Kama reborn and raises him as her own.
source_excerpt: A great fish swallowed the infant and was caught by fishermen and given to Shambara; the cook found the child in its belly and gave him to Mayavati, who — being Rati, Kama's wife — knew him and raised him, later revealing he was Krishna's son and her own destined husband. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 3-14)

title: Pradyumna Slays Shambara
one_line_summary: Armed with the great science of countering illusion, Pradyumna challenges and beheads the demon Shambara.
source_excerpt: Mayavati gave Pradyumna the Maha-vidya that destroys all illusion; Pradyumna challenged Shambara, countered his hundred forms of maya, and with his sharp sword cut off the demon's head. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 15-23)

title: Pradyumna Returns to Dvaraka and Is Recognized
one_line_summary: Pradyumna returns to Dvaraka with Mayavati; Rukmini recognizes her long-lost son, and the city rejoices.
source_excerpt: Pradyumna entered the inner apartments with his wife; Rukmini, sensing her lost son, wondered at his resemblance to Krishna, and when Narada told the whole tale, Rukmini, Devaki and Vasudeva embraced the couple in joy, and Dvaraka celebrated him as one returned from the dead. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-39)

title: Surya Gives Satrajit the Syamantaka Jewel
one_line_summary: Surya gives his devotee Satrajit the Syamantaka jewel, which yields eight loads of gold daily and makes him shine like the sun.
source_excerpt: Pleased with his devotee Satrajit, Surya gave him the Syamantaka jewel; wearing it, Satrajit shone like the sun, so the people of Dvaraka mistook him for the sun-god; the jewel yielded eight loads of gold daily and warded off all calamity. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-10)

title: Satrajit Refuses Krishna; Prasena Is Slain
one_line_summary: Satrajit refuses to hand the jewel to Krishna; his brother Prasena, wearing it on a hunt, is killed by a lion, and rumor blames Krishna.
source_excerpt: Though Krishna asked for the jewel, the covetous Satrajit refused; his brother Prasena, wearing it on a hunt, was slain by a lion, which was in turn slain by Jambavan, and the people whispered that Krishna had killed Prasena for the jewel. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-15)

title: Krishna Fights Jambavan for the Jewel
one_line_summary: To clear his name, Krishna traces Prasena's path, enters Jambavan's cave, and fights the bear-king for twenty-eight days before Jambavan yields the jewel and his daughter.
source_excerpt: Krishna, tracing Prasena's trail, entered the bear's dark cave and fought Jambavan day and night for twenty-eight days with fists like thunderbolts; Jambavan, exhausted, recognized him as Vishnu, the ancient Lord, and gave him the jewel along with his daughter Jambavati. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 16-31)

title: Krishna Clears His Name and Returns the Jewel
one_line_summary: Krishna returns with the jewel and Jambavati, clears his name in open assembly, and returns the Syamantaka to Satrajit, who also offers Satyabhama.
source_excerpt: Krishna returned with the jewel and his bride, recounted all in the assembly, and restored the Syamantaka to Satrajit; ashamed, Satrajit gave Krishna his daughter Satyabhama along with the jewel, but Krishna accepted only the bride and returned the jewel to its owner. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 32-44)

title: Satadhanva Slays Satrajit for the Jewel
one_line_summary: Instigated by Akrura and Kritavarma, Satadhanva murders the sleeping Satrajit and steals the Syamantaka jewel.
source_excerpt: While Krishna was away, Akrura and Kritavarma urged Satadhanva to seize the jewel, saying Satrajit had broken his word; the wicked Satadhanva slew the sleeping Satrajit and made off with the Syamantaka. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-5)

title: Satyabhama Reports Her Father's Murder
one_line_summary: Satyabhama finds her father slain, and hastens to Hastinapura to tell Krishna, who laments with Balarama.
source_excerpt: Satyabhama, seeing her father killed, wailed 'father, father, I am slain'; she laid his body in a vat of oil and went to Hastinapura to tell Krishna, who, hearing it, wept with Balarama. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 6-8)

title: Krishna Slays Satadhanva but Finds No Jewel
one_line_summary: Krishna pursues and beheads Satadhanva near Mithila but finds no jewel; Balarama goes on to visit King Janaka.
source_excerpt: Krishna and Rama pursued Satadhanva, who fled a hundred yojanas on horseback; Krishna beheaded him with his discus, but searching him found no jewel; Balarama then went on to Mithila to visit Janaka, where he stayed some months and taught Duryodhana the mace. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-25)

title: Krishna Recovers the Jewel from Akrura
one_line_summary: Krishna reveals that Satadhanva had left the jewel with Akrura; Akrura produces it, and Krishna returns it to him after showing it to his kinsmen.
source_excerpt: Krishna, who knew all, told Akrura the jewel had been entrusted to him; Akrura produced the Syamantaka, and Krishna showed it to his kinsmen to wipe away the stain of suspicion, then returned the jewel to Akrura. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-40)

title: Krishna Visits the Pandavas at Indraprastha
one_line_summary: Krishna visits the Pandavas at Indraprastha, is joyously received by Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Draupadi and Kunti, and stays four months.
source_excerpt: Krishna came to Indraprastha to see the Pandavas; they rose at once, embraced him, and Kunti, weeping with love, said 'now we are protected, for you remember us.' Krishna stayed four months, delighting all. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-11)

title: Krishna Weds Kalindi at the Yamuna
one_line_summary: While hunting with Arjuna, Krishna meets Kalindi, daughter of the Sun, doing penance at the Yamuna, and later weds her.
source_excerpt: Arjuna, sent by Krishna, asked the beautiful maiden her name; she said 'I am Kalindi, daughter of Surya, doing penance to win Vishnu as husband'; Krishna took her on his chariot and later wed her at an auspicious time. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 12-28)

title: Krishna Grants the Khadava Forest to Agni
one_line_summary: Krishna, as Arjuna's charioteer, helps him give the Khadava forest to Agni, who bestows the Gandiva bow and inexhaustible quivers.
source_excerpt: Dwelling there for the Pandavas' good, Krishna acted as Arjuna's charioteer when Arjuna gave the Khadava forest to Agni; pleased, Agni gave Arjuna the Gandiva bow, inexhaustible quivers and an invincible chariot, and the rescued Maya built the assembly hall. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 23-26)

title: Krishna Abducts Mitravinda and Wins Satya
one_line_summary: Krishna carries off Mitravinda of Avanti from her svayamvara and wins Satya of Kosala by taming seven fierce bulls.
source_excerpt: Krishna forcibly carried off Mitravinda, the princess of Avanti, before the assembled kings; and to win Satya, daughter of Nagnajit of Kosala, he multiplied himself sevenfold and with ease subdued seven untamable bulls, winning the princess. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 29-55)

title: Krishna Weds Bhadra and Abducts Lakshmana
one_line_summary: Krishna weds Bhadra, daughter of his aunt, and carries off Lakshmana of Madra from her svayamvara.
source_excerpt: Krishna wed Bhadra, daughter of his aunt Srutakirti, given by her brothers; and he carried off Lakshmana, the fair daughter of the king of Madra, from her svayamvara like Garuda seizing nectar. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 55-57)

title: Krishna Breaches Mura's Fortifications
one_line_summary: Indra complains of Narakasura's thefts; Krishna with Satyabhama on Garuda shatters the mountain, weapon, water, fire and Mura-pasha defenses of Pragjyotisha.
source_excerpt: Indra, robbed of his umbrella, earrings and the Amara hill, complained to Krishna; riding Garuda with Satyabhama, Krishna broke the mountains with his mace, the weapon-forts with arrows, the fire and water with his discus, and Mura's nooses with his sword. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-5)

title: Krishna Slays Mura and His Seven Sons
one_line_summary: Krishna beheads the five-headed demon Mura and slays his seven sons who attack in revenge.
source_excerpt: Mura, roused by Krishna's conch, rose from the waters with five heads and hurled his trident; Krishna shattered it with two arrows and with his discus cut off Mura's heads, then slew Mura's seven sons who attacked to avenge their father. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 5-14)

title: Krishna Slays Narakasura
one_line_summary: Krishna beheads the demon king Narakasura (Bhauma) with his discus, freeing the three worlds of his tyranny.
source_excerpt: As Narakasura raised his spear, Krishna cut off his head with the sharp-edged discus, and it fell to earth decked with earrings and crown, while the sages and gods showered flowers in praise. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-22)

title: Bhumi Returns Aditi's Earrings
one_line_summary: The earth-goddess Bhumi restores Aditi's earrings and Varuna's umbrella and prays for the protection of Naraka's son Bhagadatta.
source_excerpt: Bhumi, the earth, came before Krishna and offered the earrings of Aditi, Varuna's umbrella and the great jewel, and praying, begged Krishna to protect her son Bhagadatta; Krishna granted him fearlessness. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 22-31)

title: Krishna Liberates the Sixteen Thousand Princesses
one_line_summary: Krishna enters Narakasura's palace and frees the 16,100 captive princesses, who all choose him as their husband.
source_excerpt: In Narakasura's palace Krishna saw the 16,100 royal princesses the demon had seized; seeing him, they all mentally chose him as their husband, and Krishna sent them to Dvaraka with vast treasures and sixty-four white elephants. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-36)

title: Satyabhama Wins the Parijata Tree
one_line_summary: Krishna returns Aditi's earrings to the gods, and at Satyabhama's wish uproots the Parijata tree from Indra's heaven, defeating the gods.
source_excerpt: Krishna returned the earrings to Aditi and was worshipped by Indra; urged by Satyabhama, he uprooted the Parijata tree, overcame Indra and the gods, and brought it to Dvaraka, planting it in Satyabhama's garden. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 37-40)

title: Krishna Marries the Sixteen Thousand Princesses
one_line_summary: Krishna, expanding into as many forms, simultaneously weds the 16,100 princesses, giving each a palace and household.
source_excerpt: In a single moment Krishna, assuming as many forms, wed all the princesses, each in her own palace, living with them as a householder would, though none but the Lord could perform such a feat. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 41-44)

title: Krishna Jests with Rukmini
one_line_summary: Krishna playfully tells Rukmini she chose a poor, unworthy husband; she faints in grief, thinking he means to abandon her.
source_excerpt: Krishna jestingly told Rukmini she had foolishly chosen a penniless husband when great kings sought her, and should choose a worthy kshatriya instead; believing him in earnest, Rukmini fainted, her fan falling from her hand. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-27)

title: Krishna Consoles Rukmini
one_line_summary: Krishna lifts Rukmini, reveals his jest, praises her devotion, and the two are reconciled in love.
source_excerpt: Krishna, seeing her distress, raised her, wiped her tears and said 'I spoke in jest to hear your words'; Rukmini answered with loving devotion, and Krishna praised her faithfulness, and they enjoyed each other's company. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 28-58)

title: Rukmi Gives His Granddaughter to Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Setting aside his grudge for his sister Rukmini's sake, Rukmi weds his granddaughter Rocana to Aniruddha in Bhojakata.
source_excerpt: Though he still nursed enmity against Krishna, Rukmi, to please his sister Rukmini, gave his granddaughter Rocana in marriage to Aniruddha, and at that wedding Rukmini, Rama, Krishna and the other Yadavas went to Bhojakata. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-26)

title: Balarama Slays Rukmi at the Dice Game
one_line_summary: At the wedding, Rukmi cheats Balarama at dice and insults him; enraged, Balarama kills Rukmi with his iron club.
source_excerpt: Urged by the Kalinga king, Rukmi played dice with Balarama; when Rukmi falsely claimed victory, a heavenly voice declared Balarama the winner, but Rukmi jeered that cowherds cannot play dice; enraged, Balarama struck him down with his club, and Krishna said nothing, fearing to wound Rukmini. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-39)

title: Bana's Thousand Arms and Shiva's Boon
one_line_summary: The thousand-armed asura Bana, son of Bali and devotee of Shiva, wins the boon of a worthy rival in battle.
source_excerpt: Bana, eldest son of Bali, pleased Shiva with his thousand arms and asked for a rival worthy of him; Shiva declared that when Bana's flag fell, his pride would be humbled in battle with a peer. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-10)

title: Usha Dreams of Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Bana's daughter Usha dreams of a beloved youth, and her friend Chitralekha paints the princes to identify him as Aniruddha.
source_excerpt: Usha dreamt of a dark, lotus-eyed youth and woke crying 'where is my beloved?'; her friend Chitralekha, skilled in art, painted the gods and princes, and Usha shyly recognized Aniruddha, Krishna's grandson. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-21)

title: Chitralekha Brings Aniruddha to Usha
one_line_summary: Chitralekha, by her mystic power, carries the sleeping Aniruddha to Shonitapura, where he lives secretly with Usha.
source_excerpt: Chitralekha flew to Dvaraka and by her yogic power brought the sleeping Aniruddha to Shonitapura; Usha, overjoyed, enjoyed his company in the guarded inner palace, and the days passed unperceived. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 21-25)

title: Bana Captures Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Bana's guards discover the secret union; Bana finds Aniruddha with Usha and binds him with serpent-nooses.
source_excerpt: The guards reported Usha's defilement; Bana, enraged, rushed to the women's quarters and found Aniruddha playing dice with his daughter, and the furious demon bound him with serpent-nooses, while Usha wept in grief. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-34)

title: Krishna Battles Shiva at Shonitapura
one_line_summary: The Vrishnis besiege Shonitapura; Shiva and Skanda fight for Bana, and Krishna repels Shiva's celestial weapons.
source_excerpt: Pradyumna, Satyaki, Gada and Samba with twelve armies besieged Shonitapura; Shiva, mounted on Nandi with his hosts, fought for Bana, and Krishna countered Shiva's Brahma, wind, fire and Pashupata weapons with matching astras. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-12)

title: Krishna Stupefies Shiva and Fells Bana's Host
one_line_summary: Krishna throws the Jrimbhana astra, stupefying Shiva, and Pradyumna routs Skanda, while Bana's mother shields her son.
source_excerpt: Krishna, stupefying Shiva with the Jrimbhana weapon, slew Bana's army, while Pradyumna's arrows drove the bloodied Skanda from the field; Bana's mother Kotara stood naked before Krishna to save her son's life. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 13-20)

title: Krishna Spares Bana at Shiva's Plea
one_line_summary: Krishna severs Bana's thousand arms with his discus; Shiva intercedes, and Krishna spares Bana with four arms remaining.
source_excerpt: Krishna cut off Bana's thousand arms with his discus as if pruning branches; Shiva pleaded for his devotee, and Krishna, honoring the boon given to Prahrada, spared Bana, leaving him four arms and freedom from fear. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 20-48)

title: Aniruddha and Usha Are Freed
one_line_summary: Bana surrenders, gives Aniruddha and Usha to Krishna, and the Vrishnis return in triumph to Dvaraka.
source_excerpt: Obtaining fearlessness, Bana bowed to Krishna, placed Aniruddha and his bride Usha on a chariot, and sent them with an army; Krishna entered Dvaraka amid conches and drums, greeted by the citizens. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 49-52)

title: Krishna Liberates King Nriga from a Lizard's Body
one_line_summary: The Yadu princes find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna pulls it out with his left hand, and it becomes the radiant King Nriga.
source_excerpt: The Yadu princes, thirsty, found a mountain-sized lizard in a dry well and could not pull it out with their ropes; Krishna came and with his left hand drew it out, and it became a being of molten-gold splendor. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

title: Nriga's Story of the Disputed Cow
one_line_summary: Nriga, an Ikshvaku king famed for charity, tells how he unwittingly gave one brahmana's stray cow to another and was cursed to become a lizard.
source_excerpt: Nriga, a great giver of cows, told how a stray cow of one brahmana got mixed into his herd and was given to another; both brahmanas claimed it and refused all compensation, and Yama, giving him the choice, made him first suffer his sin, so he fell as a lizard. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-23)

title: Nriga Ascends and Krishna Warns Against Stealing Brahmanas' Wealth
one_line_summary: Touched by Krishna, Nriga ascends to heaven in a celestial car, and Krishna warns the citizens that a brahmana's property is deadly poison.
source_excerpt: Nriga praised Krishna, bowed, and ascended to heaven in a celestial car; Krishna then taught the people that a brahmana's wealth is like poison — it consumes a king and his family for generations. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-43)

title: Balarama Visits the Gopis of Gokula
one_line_summary: Balarama returns to Nanda's Gokula, consoles the pining gopis with Krishna's message, and stays two months in their company.
source_excerpt: Balarama went to Nanda's Gokula, was embraced by the gopas and gopis, and consoled the gopis, who asked after Krishna, with Krishna's heart-felt messages; he stayed two months, sporting with them in the Yamuna groves. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-17)
notes: Balarama-centered episode within the Krishna cycle; Krishna is present only through the message delivered.

title: Balarama Drags the Yamuna with His Plough
one_line_summary: Intoxicated by Varuni, Balarama summons the Yamuna to sport; when she refuses, he drags her with his plough until she begs forgiveness.
source_excerpt: Drinking the Varuni that flowed from a tree, Balarama, intoxicated, summoned the Yamuna to sport with him; when she did not come, he dragged her with the tip of his plough, and the frightened river, bowing, begged his pardon, after which he released her and bathed. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 18-33)
notes: Balarama-centered episode; the plough-drag of the Yamuna is a celebrated feat attributed to Balarama (Halayudha).

title: Paundraka Falsely Claims to Be Vasudeva
one_line_summary: Paundraka, king of Karusha, proclaims himself the true Vasudeva and sends a messenger demanding that Krishna surrender his divine insignia.
source_excerpt: Paundraka, deluded into believing himself Vasudeva, sent a messenger to Krishna demanding he give up the divine marks he wore; the assembly laughed, and Krishna replied that he would hurl those signs at the fool and slay him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-9)

title: Krishna Slays Paundraka and the King of Kashi
one_line_summary: Krishna marches to Kashi, beheads the impostor Paundraka with his discus, and casts the head of the Kashi king into his own city.
source_excerpt: Krishna, seeing Paundraka arrayed in counterfeit divine dress, laughed, then with sharp arrows and his discus cut off Paundraka's head and the Kashi king's head, casting the latter into the city of Kashi. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-24)

title: Sudarshana Destroys the Abhichara Fire and Varanasi
one_line_summary: Sudakshina conjures a fiery demon by black magic to kill Krishna; Krishna's Sudarshana discus destroys it and burns Varanasi.
source_excerpt: Sudakshina, son of the Kashi king, worshipped Shiva and by abhichara rites raised a terrible fire-demon; Krishna sent his Sudarshana discus, which destroyed the demon, burned Sudakshina and his priests, and reduced Varanasi to ashes. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 25-42)

title: The Gorilla Dvivida Ravages the Land
one_line_summary: The gorilla Dvivida, Narakasura's friend, wreaks havoc on the countryside in revenge, burning villages, drowning lands and defiling sages' hermitages.
source_excerpt: Dvivida, the mighty ape and friend of Narakasura, seeking vengeance, set fire to cities and villages, uprooted mountains, drowned the coastal lands, and defiled the sages' hermitages and sacred fires. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

title: Balarama Slays the Gorilla Dvivida
one_line_summary: The ape Dvivida insults Balarama and his women; Balarama fells him with his mace, freeing the land of the menace.
source_excerpt: Dvivida, seeing Balarama sporting on Raivataka, mocked him and his women; Balarama, enraged, struck him with his mace, and the ape, after hurling trees and rocks in vain, was felled, vomiting blood, as gods rained flowers. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-27)
notes: Balarama-centered episode within the Krishna cycle.

title: Samba Abducts Lakshmana and Is Captured
one_line_summary: Samba carries off Lakshmana, Duryodhana's daughter, from her svayamvara; the Kauravas fight him and take him captive.
source_excerpt: Samba, son of Jambavati, carried off Lakshmana, daughter of Duryodhana, from her svayamvara; Karna, Shala, Bhuri and Duryodhana fought him, and though Samba wounded them all, they surrounded and captured him with great effort. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-12)

title: Balarama Seeks Samba's Release and Is Insulted
one_line_summary: Balarama goes to Hastinapura as peacemaker, but the Kauravas, drunk on pride, mock the Yadavas and refuse to release Samba.
source_excerpt: Balarama, restraining the war-eager Vrishnis, went to Hastinapura and asked for Samba's release; the Kauravas mocked the Yadavas as cowherds who had risen above their station, and refused, insulting Balarama. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 13-38)

title: Balarama Drags Hastinapura with His Plough
one_line_summary: Enraged, Balarama seizes his plough and drags the city of Hastinapura toward the Ganga; the terrified Kauravas surrender Samba and Lakshmana.
source_excerpt: Balarama, declaring he would make the earth free of Kauravas, dug his plough into Hastinapura and dragged it toward the Ganga; the Kauravas, terrified, surrendered Samba and Lakshmana, and Duryodhana gave rich gifts as the city was released. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 39-53)

title: Narada Sees Krishna in Every Palace of Dvaraka
one_line_summary: Narada visits Dvaraka to witness Krishna's household, and sees him simultaneously present in each of the 16,000 palaces performing different duties.
source_excerpt: Narada, curious how Krishna wed 16,000 wives with one body, entered palace after palace and saw Krishna everywhere at once — playing dice, raising children, performing sacrifices, worshipping, hunting — in each of the 16,000 mansions. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-38)

title: Narada Marvels at Krishna's Yoga-Maya and Departs
one_line_summary: Narada praises Krishna's unfathomable yoga-maya, and Krishna bids him wander singing his glories throughout the worlds.
source_excerpt: Narada, amazed, declared 'I understand your yoga-maya, hard to see even for the master of maya, revealed to me by serving your feet'; Krishna bade him roam the worlds singing his purifying pastimes, and Narada departed remembering him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 36-44)
